trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Aerobus (€6.75) or Metro L9 Sud to the city center and check into Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a self-guided walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — see Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside for free. Grab a coffee and soak in the Modernista architecture of the Eixample grid streets.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the nearby Rambla de Catalunya for a relaxed evening atmosphere. Explore the Eixample neighborhood bars and enjoy the start of Barcelona's famous nightlife at a local bar with €2–3 cañas (draft beers) during happy hour.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and croissant at the airport (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Mercado de l'Abaceria or a local bocadillo shop near Eixample — budget €5–8 for a sandwich and drink
meals.dinner: Bar Calders or a neighborhood tapas bar in Eixample — order patatas bravas, pan con tomate, and croquetas. Budget €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: August is peak season — stay hydrated, wear sunscreen, and carry a reusable water bottle. Public fountains offer free drinking water. Validate your metro ticket on arrival for easy transport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Sagrada Família. Book tickets online in advance (€26 basic entry) to avoid long queues. Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring Gaudí's masterpiece — the exterior is stunning even if budget is tight, but interior is worth the splurge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take Metro L2/L5 to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic). Explore the narrow medieval streets, visit the free Barcelona Cathedral exterior, Plaça Reial, and Pont del Bisbe for free. Duck into small plazas and hidden courtyards.
day_by_day.evening: Head to El Born neighborhood adjacent to the Gothic Quarter. Browse the trendy streets and join the nightlife scene — El Born is known for creative cocktail bars and a young crowd. Many bars offer free entrance and affordable drinks.

meals.breakfast: Granja Viader or any local cafeteria near the hotel — café amb llet and toast with tomato for €3–5
meals.lunch: Mercat de Santa Caterina (less touristy than La Boqueria) — grab fresh fruit, cheese, and a bocadillo for €6–9
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — a classic cava bar with affordable tapas. Budget €12–16 per person including drinks

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot. Watch for pickpockets in crowded areas. Many churches and plazas are free to enter or view from outside.

day_by_day.morning: Take Metro L3 to Paral·lel and ride the free funicular up to Montjuïc. Visit the free Jardins de Laribal and enjoy panoramic views of Barcelona. Walk to the Fundació Joan Miró (€14 entry) or admire the Montjuïc Castle exterior for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Barceloneta beach via Metro or a scenic walk. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach (free), swim in the Mediterranean, and explore the Barceloneta neighborhood. Walk along the Port Olímpic waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample or head to Gràcia neighborhood for the evening. August 15–21 is the famous Festa Major de Gràcia — streets are decorated with elaborate themes and there are FREE concerts, activities, and a festive atmosphere throughout the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café or a local bakery near Eixample — avocado toast or pastry with coffee for €4–7
meals.lunch: Barceloneta beachfront chiringuito (beach bar) — grilled fish or paella. Look for a menú del día (set lunch menu) for €12–15 including bread, drink, and dessert
meals.dinner: Gràcia neighborhood during Festa Major — street food stalls and local vendors offer affordable bites for €5–10. Grab a beer and enjoy the free live music

day_by_day.notes: Festa Major de Gràcia (August 15–21) is one of Barcelona's best free festivals — streets are elaborately decorated by residents and there are free concerts nightly. Don't miss this if your dates align!

day_by_day.morning: Visit Park Güell — book the Monumental Zone tickets in advance (€10). Arrive early (opening time) to beat the crowds and heat. The park's free zones with city views are equally impressive and worth exploring after your ticketed visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill from Park Güell through the Gràcia neighborhood. Browse the charming Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia — local squares with a relaxed vibe. Visit the Mercat de l'Abaceria (free entry) and explore boutique shops and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife. Head to Eixample's 'Gayxample' area or Carrer del Consell de Cent for pre-drinks at affordable bars. Then head to a club like Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz (entry €10–15, often with a drink included). Clubs typically fill up after midnight.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh orange juice and croissant from a local mercat or bakery in Gràcia — €3–5
meals.lunch: Menú del día at a local restaurant in Gràcia — 3-course meal with wine for €11–14. Look for handwritten chalkboard menus outside
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca near Eixample — popular spot for pintxos and tapas. Budget €13–18 per person. Go early (7–8 PM) to avoid long waits

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed entry slots sell out weeks in advance in August — book as early as possible. Wear comfortable shoes as the walk uphill is steep. For nightlife, note that Barcelona clubs stay open until 5–6 AM; pace yourself!

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit Palau de la Música Catalana, a UNESCO World Heritage Modernista concert hall. Guided tours cost €22 or attend a morning concert for a similar price. Alternatively, admire the stunning facade for free from the outside on Carrer de Sant Pere Més Alt.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last stroll through El Raval neighborhood — visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art Barcelona) exterior, a popular skate spot. Browse the weekend market at Mercat de Sant Antoni (open daily, great for vintage finds and local produce). Pick up affordable souvenirs at local shops rather than tourist traps.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample close to the hotel. Enjoy a final glass of cava or vermouth at a rooftop bar or local terrace. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume or any local pastry shop — ensaïmada (traditional pastry) and coffee for €3–5
meals.lunch: Mercat de Sant Antoni — grab fresh produce, cheese, and local snacks for a picnic-style farewell lunch for €7–10
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda or similar neighborhood wine bar near Eixample — tapas and a bottle of house wine shared. Budget €14–18 per person for a relaxed, authentic farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Keep track of your departure time and factor in airport transfer (45–60 min via Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud). Aerobus departs from Plaça de Catalunya. August traffic can be heavy — allow extra time. Store luggage at the hotel until your departure if needed.

trip_options.title: Classic Barcelona Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Travel from airport to hotel in Eixample via Aerobus or metro (Line L9 Sud). Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay, freshen up, and get oriented in the Eixample neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — Gaudí's Casa Batlló, Domènech i Montaner's Casa Lleó Morera, and Puig i Cadafalch's Casa Amatller from the outside. This is a perfect low-effort, high-reward introduction to Barcelona's modernista architecture, all within walking distance of the hotel. Pick up a coffee and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the El Born neighborhood for a relaxed first evening. Explore the atmospheric streets, pop into a local bar for a welcome vermouth, and enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bocadillo or menú del día at a café near the hotel after check-in — try any local bar on Carrer del Consell de Cent for a €12–15 set lunch.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet on Carrer de Montcada in El Born — a beloved traditional cava bar serving classic tapas like anchovies, jamón, and patatas bravas. Budget around €25–35 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 13:00, allow at least 90 minutes for baggage, transit, and hotel check-in before planning any activities. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Book Sagrada Família tickets online tonight if not already done — they sell out weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour (9:00–11:30 AM). Start the day with the crown jewel of Barcelona architecture. The skip-the-line guided tour offers deep insight into Gaudí's vision, the symbolism of the facades, and the breathtaking interior forest of columns. Book the tower access add-on for panoramic city views. The basilica is a short metro or taxi ride from Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration (1:00–5:00 PM). After lunch, head uphill to Park Güell. Explore the UNESCO-listed monumental zone — the mosaic dragon staircase, Hypostyle Room, and the sweeping terrace with views over the city. Afterward, wind down through the charming Gràcia neighborhood below, browsing its boutique shops and plaza culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for dinner and an early taste of Barcelona's nightlife. Explore the Eixample Esquerra area, known locally as 'Gayxample,' with a vibrant bar scene. Enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar before heading to bed at a reasonable hour to pace yourself for the week.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try Forn de Sant Jaume on Rambla de Catalunya for fresh pastries and coffee (€6–9).
meals.lunch: After Sagrada Família, grab lunch near the Sagrada Família metro stop. Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca is a local favorite for tapas and montaditos (€20–30 per person).
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample — a cozy wine bar and restaurant with excellent Catalan dishes and a great wine list. Expect €30–40 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: August is peak season — Park Güell's monumental zone requires timed-entry tickets purchased in advance (€10). Morning slots sell out fast; book online before the trip. Wear comfortable shoes as Park Güell involves uphill walking. Stay hydrated — August in Barcelona is very hot (30°C+).

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour (10:00 AM – 12:30 PM). Dive into Barcelona's medieval heart with a small-group or self-guided tour of the Barri Gòtic. Discover Roman walls, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden alleyways dating back 2,000 years. Download the Rick Steves or GPSmyCity app for a self-guided option to keep costs down, or book a €15–20 small-group tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas & Vermouth Food Tour in El Born (2:00–5:30 PM). Join a guided food tour through the trendy El Born neighborhood. Sample traditional tapas, local vermouth, fresh seafood, and Catalan specialties at multiple stops. This is both a cultural and culinary deep dive, combining food with stories about the neighborhood's history and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Nightlife Experience — Passeig del Born & Barceloneta Club Scene. Begin with craft cocktails at rooftop bars along Passeig del Born as the sun sets. Move to the beachfront Barceloneta area as the night progresses, where beach clubs and open-air venues come alive after midnight. This is Barcelona's iconic nightlife circuit — pace yourself and don't expect clubs to fill up before 1:00 AM.

meals.breakfast: Bar Calders in Sant Antoni neighborhood — a classic Barcelona breakfast spot with great coffee, fresh orange juice, and toast with tomato (pa amb tomàquet). Budget €7–10.
meals.lunch: Lunch is included as part of the El Born Food Tour (typically 4–6 tasting stops covering a full meal's worth of food). Tour cost approximately €65–80 per person.
meals.dinner: Light dinner before the nightlife begins — La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, arrives early as it closes when food runs out). Famous for its original bombas and grilled seafood. Budget €20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The food tour and nightlife evening make this the most packed day — pace yourself at lunch. For the club scene, Opium Barcelona and Pacha Barcelona on the beachfront are popular mid-range options (€15–20 entry, drinks €10–15 each). Taxis back to Eixample from Barceloneta run €8–12. Keep valuables secure in the Gothic Quarter — it is a pickpocket hotspot.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the late night. Sleep in, have a slow breakfast, and take a gentle walk along Rambla de Catalunya (the more elegant, locals-preferred alternative to La Rambla). Browse the flower stalls, café terraces, and modernista architecture at a relaxed pace. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies nearby if interested in contemporary Catalan art (€12 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc Hill Exploration (2:00–6:00 PM). Take the Montjuïc cable car or funicular up to the hilltop park. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc for panoramic harbor views, explore the Jardins de Laribal, and stop by the Fundació Joan Miró (€14 entry) for world-class modern art in a beautiful rationalist building. A great architectural and cultural afternoon without the morning crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the El Born / Sant Pere area for a final evening of bar-hopping and dinner. The neighborhood has some of Barcelona's best cocktail bars and a lively but more local-feeling atmosphere compared to the tourist-heavy beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Slow brunch at Federal Café in Sant Antoni — a beloved expat and local brunch spot with excellent eggs, avocado toast, and specialty coffee. Budget €12–16.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a terrace café on Montjuïc or a picnic from a nearby Mercadona supermarket to enjoy in the Jardins de Laribal with city views. Budget €8–12.
meals.dinner: Bar del Pla in El Born — a lively Catalan tapas bar with excellent croquetas, foie gras, and local wines. Great atmosphere and honest prices. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Montjuïc Telefèric (cable car) offers stunning views and runs until 9:00 PM in summer — consider timing your descent for golden hour. If energy allows, the Magic Fountain of Montjuïc has free light and music shows on Thursday–Sunday evenings at 9:30 PM and 10:30 PM in summer — a spectacular free experience on the walk back down.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana Guided Tour (10:00 AM). A UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece by Domènech i Montaner, this concert hall is arguably the most stunning interior space in Barcelona. The guided tour (€22) reveals the stained-glass skylight, sculpted columns, and ornate stage in extraordinary detail. Book in advance — tours fill up quickly. Located just north of El Born.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon for personal exploration and shopping. Browse the boutiques of El Born and the Eixample for design goods, Spanish fashion, and souvenirs. Visit the Mercat de Santa Caterina (a colorful alternative to La Boqueria, far less touristy) for local produce and snacks. Return to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample — choose a special restaurant to close out the trip on a high note. Enjoy a final walk along the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia to admire the modernista facades lit up at night before calling it an evening.

meals.breakfast: Granja Viader near the Raval — one of Barcelona's oldest cafés, serving the original cacaolat (chocolate milk) and traditional ensaïmada pastries since 1870. Budget €8–12.
meals.lunch: Mercat de Santa Caterina food stalls for a casual, authentic market lunch — fresh seafood, local cheeses, and cured meats. Budget €15–20.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza in Eixample — a beloved local restaurant with excellent Neapolitan-style pizzas and natural wines in a stylish setting. A crowd-pleasing, mid-range farewell dinner. Budget €25–35 per person. Alternatively, splurge slightly at Honest Greens or Disfrutar (book months ahead for Disfrutar — a world top-10 restaurant).

day_by_day.notes: If departing early on Day 6, confirm hotel checkout time and arrange airport transport the night before. The Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya takes 35 minutes to the airport and costs €6.75. Allow at least 2.5 hours before flight departure for international flights. Use the final evening to revisit any favorite spots or simply soak in the Eixample atmosphere from a terrace café.

meals.dinner: Pre-club dinner at El Nacional Barcelona — a stunning multi-concept food hall in a restored 1889 building on Passeig de Gràcia, offering Catalan cuisine across multiple dining spaces.

day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sophisticated evening in El Born. Start with cocktails at Bar Paradiso (a celebrated speakeasy hidden behind a pastrami bar) and then head to a jazz or live music venue such as Jamboree Jazz Club in Plaça Reial for a premium cultural nightlife experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel's in-house restaurant or Copasetic — a stylish brunch spot near Eixample with an international menu and excellent coffee.
meals.lunch: The tapas and vermouth food tour in El Born serves as a premium grazing lunch experience across multiple stops — included in the tour.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bodega Sepúlveda or Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas bar) — book Tickets months ahead as it is one of Barcelona's most sought-after dining reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to architectural immersion along Passeig de Gràcia's 'Block of Discord.' Purchase tickets for a private guided tour inside Casa Batlló (Gaudí's dragon-scaled masterpiece) and optionally Casa Amatller or Casa Lleó Morera. Explore the interior apartment museum and the immersive Espai Gaudí exhibition in the attic. Afterward, indulge in a luxury spa session at the hotel or a nearby premium wellness center to recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Barcelona's elite nightlife scene. Begin with a sunset aperitivo at Eclipse Bar atop the W Barcelona hotel (panoramic Mediterranean views), then experience a world-class DJ set at Soho House Barcelona's rooftop or a curated private event at one of the city's exclusive members' clubs.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel gourmet breakfast or visit Forn de Sant Josep — an iconic Barcelona bakery on Rambla de Catalunya for artisan pastries and café con leche.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Eixample institution renowned for its montaditos, fresh seafood tapas, and craft beers.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cinc Sentits (one Michelin star, modern Catalan tasting menu) in Eixample — an intimate, world-class dining experience celebrating local seasonal ingredients.

Hotel concierge can assist with W Barcelona Eclipse Bar reservations and nightlife access.
